messages.content: Help me determine if the system property 'enableXmlSecurityFeature' is set to enable the security feature 'XML_SECURITY' in a Java XML processing environment?

function.name: JdkXmlFeatures_getSystemProperty
function.description: Checks if the specified system property is set and applies its boolean value to the given XML feature. Throws NumberFormatException if the property value is invalid. Note that the provided function is in Java 8 SDK syntax.

feature.description: The XML feature to check the system property for. This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation.

sysPropertyName.description: The name of the system property to be checked. This is Java String type parameter in string representation.

message.reasoning: The user wants to determine if the system property 'enableXmlSecurityFeature' is set to enable the security feature 'XML_SECURITY' in a Java XML processing environment. They want to use the function JdkXmlFeatures_getSystemProperty. The function signature: JdkXmlFeatures_getSystemProperty takes an object with fields: feature (string), sysPropertyName (string). It returns any. We need to call the function with feature: "XML_SECURITY" and sysPropertyName: "enableXmlSecurityFeature". Then we need to interpret the result. The function will throw NumberFormatException if the property value is invalid. But we don't know the actual system property value. We can simulate calling the function. The function returns a boolean or throws exception. We need to handle that. So we should call the function and then interpret the returned boolean. If it's true, then the feature is enabled. If false, not enabled. If exception thrown, then property value is invalid. So we need to call the function.
